It does not perform any network operations, file exfiltration, or execute external payloads. The `eval` usage, while potentially risky in general, here only constructs standard `package_*` functions using predefined arrays and string manipulations that reference local, statically defined variables and paths. All data used is embedded directly in the PKGBUILD and relates to known OpenTelemetry components from the official GitHub repository.

There is no command substitution, no external downloads, no use of `curl`, `wget`, `base64`, or `eval` on remote content. The `sed` usage is limited to local string parsing for path extraction and poses no risk in this context.

Therefore, even though `main` is called at the top level, it only preps packaging functions and does not trigger any unsafe operations during `--printsrcinfo`.
</details>
